correctness.rationale: Each block of q+1 positions supplies an equal pair; concatenation preserves the run condition, including when adjacent chosen runs merge. For the odd threshold, reserve a final 2q+1 positions to force a triple, and take pairs in the preceding r−1 blocks. Thus the universal lengths 2r and 2r+1 are guaranteed at (q+1)r and (q+1)r+q. In the cyclic source, greedy embeddings minimize each selected index. An LDS of length L with r maximal runs has first index of appearance 1+x₁+q(L−r)+Σδᵢ≥qL−(q−1)⌊L/2⌋. This bound is attained with initial letter 0, all jumps +1, and maximal r, including for q=2 after wraparound. The resulting thresholds invert to the stated minimum, also at n≤q. The unique run decomposition weights the first letter by Σz^j (1≤j≤q), each run by z^q y²/(1−z^q y), and each distinct-letter transition by Σz^j (1≤j<q); summing the geometric series counts words, not embeddings. Multiplication by 1/(1−z) gives cumulative counts. An independent distinct-subsequence enumeration agreed for q=2,3,4,5 over all words up to n=8,7,6,5 respectively, and checked every first-appearance length cell for these four cyclic sources through n=14.
residual_risks: The supplied verifier generates formal recurrence coefficients through n=80 but compares explicit cyclic-prefix counts only at the enumeration bounds in lines 118–128. Neither that finite check nor the independent enumeration proves the unbounded formula; the run decomposition does.
The result does not classify all minimizing words or any embedding multiplicities.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact worst-case benchmark for an established subsequence optimization problem. The formula resolves the parity/residue transition beyond the disjoint-pairs bound and identifies a single family of extremizers for all q and n. The rational bivariate series separately supplies the number and lengths of feasible outputs on that extremal family, rather than just the optimizer length. Both facts apply across alphabet sizes and prefix lengths, not to a sampled or arbitrary small slice.
